idiom_name: StringBuilder / List<T> passed as a reference parameter (ref/out for reassignment)
implementation_notes: Collecting uses the BCL's accumulator classes: `System.Text.StringBuilder` for text (`Append`, `AppendLine`, `AppendJoin`) and `List<T>`/`ICollection<T>` for objects (`Add`, `AddRange`), passed to helpers that append and never return the accumulator. Because classes have reference semantics the plain parameter is enough for mutation; `ref`/`out` are only needed when the callee must replace the accumulator instance, and `in` documents read-only access. Where the producers are LINQ-shaped, `Aggregate`/`SelectMany`/`ToArray` build the result by returning values and usually read better than threading a mutable parameter.
pitfalls: A struct accumulator passed without `ref` is copied: appends land in the copy and vanish when the method returns (C# passes arguments by value by default).
LINQ's deferred execution plus a shared mutable accumulator duplicates entries: an iterator method that appends to the list is re-run on every enumeration.
`StringBuilder` is not thread-safe and `List<T>` tolerates no concurrent writes: parallel producers need per-producer accumulators plus a merge.
